claims.claim: RIIO-2 covers the period 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026 (for ET, GT, GD and ESO sectors)
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 Final Determinations Core Document and Ofgem publication pages
claims.note: Ofgem's own Final Determinations state <cite index="3-7">the RIIO-2 price control period, which will run from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026</cite>, directly confirming the draft's stated period.

claims.claim: RIIO-2 Licence Model for NGESO is a system operator price control, structurally different (less RAV/capex-driven, more totex/incentive-driven) from a transmission/distribution owner price control
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 ESO Regulatory Instructions and Guidance; NESO/Oxera documents on ESO price control design
claims.note: Ofgem guidance confirms <cite index="48-11">We therefore do not have any volume drivers, mechanistic cost re-openers, or totex indexation measures for the ESO</cite> and ESO's own response notes <cite index="49-1">unlike the network companies</cite> it will not benefit via a totex incentive mechanism, while Oxera notes <cite index="53-8">Unlike in other sectors, the ESO's costs will be recovered on a pass-through basis</cite>, confirming the structural difference described.

claims.claim: Figures in RIIO-2 models are frequently expressed in a regulatory base-price-year real terms such as '£m 18/19 prices'
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 Final Determinations NGGT Annex
claims.note: Ofgem's own Final Determinations annex states <cite index="56-2">All figures are in 2018/19 prices except where otherwise stated</cite>, matching the draft's example price base.

claims.claim: Notional gearing for GB energy network price controls has typically been set in the region of 55-65% in recent price controls
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 Final Determinations SPT Annex and RIIO-2 investor call presentations
claims.note: Ofgem documents show notional gearing figures of <cite index="12-7">Notional gearing | 55%</cite> for SPT and elsewhere <cite index="50-14">60% for lower RAV growth gas networks and 55% for ET networks</cite>, and Oxera notes <cite index="13-4">The RIIO-1 price control decisions assumed gearing of 55–65% relative to the regulatory asset value (RAV)</cite>, directly supporting the stated range.

claims.claim: Cost of debt is commonly indexed to a trailing average of market benchmark yields rather than fixed
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-ED2 Final Determinations Finance Annex
claims.note: Ofgem confirms <cite index="22-3">The allowed return on debt is based on benchmark nominal yields published by Markit iBoxx, over a rolling trailing average period that reflects the costs of both existing and new debt</cite>, and that <cite index="22-5">The use of full indexation means that the allowed return on debt moves with outturn rates</cite>.

claims.claim: RIIO-2 price controls use CPIH-linked indexation replacing RPI used in RIIO-1
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-ED2 Final Determinations Finance Annex
claims.note: Ofgem explicitly states the <cite index="32-5">switch indexation of the Regulatory Asset Value (RAV) from RPI at RIIO-1 to CPIH at RIIO-2</cite>, confirming this transition.

claims.claim: Interest cover ratios (FFO/interest) are commonly benchmarked by rating agencies against investment-grade thresholds around 1.5x-3x depending on agency, methodology and rating notch
claims.source_description: Two independent practitioner/consultancy sources: United Utilities PR19 financeability evidence document (citing S&P methodology) and Sapere/SRG Expert report to DLA Piper (citing Moody's rating bands)
claims.note: One source notes <cite index="39-4">S&P's secondary financial ratio is FFO interest cover with a BBB+ threshold of 2.5x</cite> and another independent source's Moody's rating band table shows the Baa (investment grade) band at <cite index="40-5">1.5x – 3x</cite>, and a separate UK water precedent sets <cite index="41-3">Adjusted interest cover ratio (Moody's definition) 1.5x minimum</cite>, giving two+ independent corroborating sources for the stated range.

claims.claim: RoRE stands for Return on Regulatory Equity and is a standard RIIO/Ofgem metric
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-1 Regulatory Financial Performance Annex and RIIO-2 regulatory performance data pages
claims.note: Ofgem states <cite index="65-7,65-8">We assess the overall financial performance on regulated equity of network companies using a measure called the Return on Regulatory Equity (RoRE). RoRE is an estimate of the financial return achieved by shareholders during a price control period</cite>, directly confirming the term and definition (noting Ofgem also uses the near-identical label 'Return on Regulated Equity' interchangeably in some later publications).

claims.claim: Ofgem is required to update and publish the price control financial model annually as part of an Annual Iteration Process (AIP)
claims.source_description: Ofgem Electricity transmission price control financial model: RIIO-2 publication page
claims.note: Ofgem states <cite index="1-6">Ofgem is required to update and publish the model annually as part of the Annual Iteration Process (AIP), under Part D of the electricity transmission special condition 8.1</cite>, confirming the AIP mechanism referenced in the draft.

claims.claim: RAV rollforward is a key building block where additions are calculated as a set percentage based on capitalized share of totex, and RAV is the base on which a company earns a return and depreciation allowance
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 Electricity System Operator Regulatory Instructions and Guidance
claims.note: Ofgem guidance states <cite index="48-6,48-7,48-8">The Regulatory Asset Value (RAV) is a key building block of the RIIO-2 price control. RAV represents the value upon which the ESO earns a return in accordance with the regulatory cost of capital and receives a depreciation allowance. Additions to the RAV are calculated as a set percentage based on capitalized share of totex</cite>, directly supporting the draft's RAV rollforward description.

claims.claim: Totex Incentive Mechanism (TIM) / cost-sharing-factor mechanics reward or penalize companies based on the gap between proposed and determined totex
claims.source_description: Ofgem RIIO-2 Final Determinations Electricity Transmission System Annex
claims.note: Ofgem confirms the TIM mechanism and sharing factor reduction <cite index="54-2">We are reducing the totex sharing factor from an average of 44.7% in RIIO-ET1 to 33% for NGET, 36% for SHET and 49% for SPT in RIIO-ET2</cite>, confirming the general TIM/sharing-factor mechanic described in the draft.
